brief.goal: Rebuild the contact page on the kit so that someone deciding whether to write to a stranger about a £1,500 puppy can see, on one screen, who they are writing to, what we can answer, how long a reply takes and what to put in the message — and then write it, in the one form on the page.
brief.scope: Nine entries: seven page sections — hero with the migrated photograph, trust strip, the kit enquiry form, how to reach us, what to tell us, one review and a four-row FAQ — plus the two chrome entries (the desktop dial and the mobile section sheet) whose styles this board exists to settle for the whole rebuild.
brief.done: The page states the email address, the hours, Carlisle · Cumbria and the 24-48 business hour reply window, carries the one migrated image and the one kit form, shows one review and four FAQ rows, names no telephone and no Scottish address, and comes to about 397 words with the facts-preserved gate reporting nothing missing that `dropped` does not explain.
out_of_scope: the telephone number: data/settings.json holds PHONE_PLACEHOLDER, so no number is shown anywhere on this page

the postal address, postcode and map coordinates the migrated page's legacy Place schema carried: they name a city the breeder does not operate from (Known Issue 16), and data/settings.json is town-level by design
international puppy transport, which the migrated body offers to discuss: no file on disk states a route, a price or a carrier for it
a second enquiry form or a mailto-only fallback: the form audit measures one field contract per content route, and two forms are two places an enquiry can be lost
prices per puppy and offer schema: the puppy pages own the offer, and this page links to them

angles.name: the answerable breeder
angles.hook: lead with what we can answer and how fast, put the form second, and say what to put in it

angles.name: the bare form
angles.hook: an H1, a form and a phone number, which is what all five scanned competitor pages are
angles.why_not: it is the page we already have, and it gives a reader no reason to choose us over the other five

angles.name: the sales landing page
angles.hook: treat contact as the bottom of the funnel: price, availability and a deposit button above the form
angles.why_not: nobody has spoken to us yet, and asking for money before a first reply is the opposite of the trust this page has to build

strategy.name: the answerable breeder
strategy.why: The scan found five contact pages that are a form and a mobile number, none with hours, a reply window, an FAQ or ContactPage markup; saying plainly what we answer, when, and what to tell us is both the reader's question and the whole competitive gap.
strategy.trade_off: It is a longer contact page than any competitor's, and a reader who only wants the email address has to read one heading to find it.

tool.evidence: The only figures on this page are a reply window, a deposit and a delivery band, all stated as sentences from data/settings.json; there is nothing for a reader to work out.
tool.trade_off: A delivery-cost estimator would suit the 'your town or postcode' field, but no file on disk gives distances or a rate, so it would have to invent them.

sections.heading: Contact Blue Staffy UK
sections.intent: A short, plain opening in Lisa Bright's first person: this is the one place to write to us about a blue Staffy, the form below is the quickest route, and a reply comes within 24-48 business hours. Carries the migrated photograph of a breeder helping a family through an enquiry.
sections.why: The migrated page opens on the same promise — ready to reserve or wanting more information, the family-run team is here to help — and a contact page that makes a reader scroll to find out how to reach anyone has wasted its first screen.
sections.why_source: src/pages/uk-blue-staffy-breeders-contact/index.astro — 'Whether you’re ready to reserve a puppy or need more information, our family-run breeding team … is here to help.'; data/page-map.json — the migrated H1 and the one image

sections.heading: What we can help with
sections.intent: The trust strip: the four standing facts a reader wants confirmed before they write — KC registration, the health tests, home raising, and UK delivery — rendered from the kit rather than restated as prose.
sections.why: Not one of the five UK breeder contact pages scanned restates KC registration, named health tests or delivery terms on the contact page itself, although several hold that content elsewhere on the site; putting it beside the form is the clearest gap the scan found.
sections.why_source: https://www.trojanstaffuk.com/contact and https://www.bullscaff.co.uk/contact — neither restates KC registration, health tests or delivery on its contact page (0 of 5 in the 2026-09-19 scan do); src/pages/uk-blue-staffy-breeders-contact/index.astro — 'ethical breeding practices'

sections.heading: What to tell us
sections.intent: What the form asks for and why each answer helps: your name and email so we can reply, a phone number and town if you want us to work out delivery, which puppy or the waiting list, and a message about your household.
sections.why: The migrated page asks for as much detail as possible but never says which detail, and the one competitor with a structured enquiry form qualifies the buyer by asking what home they can provide — saying out loud what each field is for is the honest version of that.
